subject: RFI: Log traceability, snapshotting, and bulk export capabilities
messages:
From: Lisa Park <lisa.park@nimbushealth.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Nimbus Health Security Team <security@nimbushealth.com>
Date: 2026-05-02T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: RFI: Log traceability & export questions

Hi Rishi / Marissa,

Thanks for agreeing to help — our InfoSec team compiled a short set of technical questions we need answered for our RFP evaluation. Could you confirm the items below and indicate whether you can provide sample exports and a brief SLA on retention/deletion timelines? We are on a compressed timeline and would like answers by end of week if possible.

1) Audit log retention: what default retention windows do you offer for admin/audit logs vs. request/telemetry logs? Can customers configure retention per-tenant?
2) Export formats: can logs be exported in bulk? Supported formats (JSON, Parquet, CSV)? Are exports point-in-time snapshots?
3) Real-time streaming: do you support streaming audit events to a customer-owned endpoint (e.g., Kinesis/Events/HTTP) and is that delivery guaranteed/durable?
4) Immutability & tamper evidence: do audit logs support write-once or append-only storage with tamper-evidence (checksums/commit hashes)?
5) Access controls & chain-of-custody: who can request exports inside Redwood and is there an auditable approval workflow?
6) Deletion and legal holds: how do you handle legal holds or customer-directed retention extensions?

Appreciate concise answers and any artifacts (sample export, retention matrix).

Regards,
Lisa Park
Procurement & Security Lead
Nimbus Health

---

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-02T11:22:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: RFI: Log traceability & export questions — need technical + legal confirmation

Team — forwarding Nimbus' questions. Draft answers below (inline). Can you review and flag any inaccuracies? Also need the three artifacts: (1) concise PDF of capabilities, (2) retention-matrix CSV, (3) sample point-in-time export JSON.

Original message quoted below.

Draft answers (please mark EDIT:):
1) Retention windows: Default admin/audit logs: 365 days; request/telemetry logs: 90 days. Customers can configure per-tenant retention up to 7 years (enterprise plan).
2) Export formats: Bulk export supported via console/API. Formats: JSON (native), Parquet (optimized), CSV (field-limited). Exports can be created as point-in-time snapshots; we surface a snapshot timestamp and TTL for the export artifact.
3) Real-time streaming: We offer delivery to customer endpoints via Kinesis, Pub/Sub, or HTTPS sink. Delivery is at-least-once with retries and a durable buffer (48–72 hours) before falling back to disk; long-term archival should use scheduled snapshots.
4) Immutability: Audit logs are stored append-only with SHA256 checksums at shard level. We can provide signed manifests for exported snapshots.
5) Access & chain-of-custody: Export requests require approval via role-based RBAC; exports are recorded in an audit trail noting approver and timestamp. Internal exports require a two-person approval for customer accounts.
6) Deletion/legal hold: We support legal holds per-customer — holds prevent deletion until released and are surfaced in Console. Deletion requests are audited and include a retention-override workflow for compliance teams.

Karthik: confirm the checksum/manifest language and streaming buffer durations.
Laura: confirm legal-hold wording & any constraints on retention maximums (we have contract limits).
Marissa: I'll need the external-facing PDF and the retention CSV for the attachment.

Thanks — R

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-02T13:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: RFI: Log traceability & export questions — need technical + legal confirmation

Rishi — quick technical confirmations and small edits:

- Retention: defaults are correct. Note: request-level telemetry (inference request logs) are configurable per-model routing and can also be tiered (hot 14 days, warm 90 days, archive configurable up to 7 years) — I'll add language that we recommend scheduled archival for long-term.
- Exports: supported formats are JSON and Parquet for full fidelity; CSV is supported but will only include flattened fields (call it "summary CSV"). Exports are created as immutable snapshot blobs; each snapshot has a manifest (signed by Redwood's HSM) that includes SHA256 checksums per-file.
- Streaming: We provide at-least-once and optionally exactly-once delivery to Kafka/PubSub via our connector when customers opt in; our default managed sinks are at-least-once with a 72-hour durable buffer and retry queue. For exact ordering guarantees customers can use our dedicated connector in Dedicated/Private modes.
- Immutability: append-only storage with periodic signed manifests — good to note manifest signing is via HSM and includes timestamp + root hash.

I'll attach the sample export and the retention CSV (poking in sample fields).

-Karthik
Principal Infra Engineer

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Fwd: RFI: Log traceability & export questions — need technical + legal confirmation

All — legal/pricing notes:
- Retention maximum: enterprise contracts can set retention up to 7 years. For Hosted customers we require a signed Data Retention Addendum for >5 year retention due to storage and audit obligations.
- Legal holds: we will surface holds via an API and Console flag. Holds bypass scheduled deletion but do not prevent customer-initiated exports. Release of hold requires authorization by customer admin plus a Redwood legal contact for disputes.
- Approvals: two-person internal approval for any internal-initiated export tied to customer data — we'll include this in the PDF.

Marissa — confirm there are no commercial objections to the retention addendum language.

Laura
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: RFI: Log traceability & export questions — final answers + artifacts attached

Hi Lisa — please find our consolidated responses below and attached artifacts (redwood-log-export-capabilities.pdf, retention-matrix-2026.csv, sample-audit-snapshot.json). I've also added a Drive link in case you want the source CSV. If you need any of these as a signed statement for your procurement pack, let me know and we can provide formal attestation.

Answers (concise):
1) Retention windows
- Admin/audit logs (account activity, admin actions): default 365 days; configurable per tenant up to 7 years for enterprise customers. Hosted customers requesting >5 years require a Data Retention Addendum.
- Request/telemetry logs (inference requests, token-level telemetry): default 90 days; tiered hot/warm/archive options available, archival configurable up to 7 years.

2) Bulk export formats & snapshotting
- Supported export formats: JSON (full-fidelity), Parquet (analytics-optimized), CSV (summary).
- Exports are created as point-in-time immutable snapshots. Each snapshot includes a signed manifest with per-file SHA256 checksums and a snapshot timestamp. Snapshots are downloadable from Console/API and optionally written to a customer-owned S3/Kinesis/PubSub sink.

3) Real-time streaming
- Supported: Kinesis, Pub/Sub, Kafka, HTTPS sinks. Managed sinks are at-least-once with a 72-hour durable buffer; dedicated connectors (Dedicated/Private customers) can be configured for stronger ordering/exactly-once semantics.

4) Immutability & tamper evidence
- Logs are stored append-only. Snapshots are published with signed manifests (HSM-signed root hash + per-file SHA256). We can provide manifest verification tooling and sample signed manifests.

5) Access controls & chain-of-custody
- Exports require role-based approvals. Internal-initiated exports for customer data need two-person approval; all export actions are logged and visible in the audit trail (who/when/reason).

6) Deletion & legal holds
- We support customer-directed legal holds which suspend deletion. Holds are exposed via Console/API; release requires customer admin action and is recorded in the audit log. Deletion requests and retention overrides are audited.

Artifacts attached:
- redwood-log-export-capabilities.pdf (concise capability summary)
- retention-matrix-2026.csv (default and configurable retention per log class)
- sample-audit-snapshot.json (sample point-in-time export with manifest header)
